b: A moated brick castle you go inside: drawbridges, the dungeon cells where the d'Este princes were locked up, painted ceilings, and the Torre dei Leoni tower climb.
g: On the Rome→Venice train day — Ferrara is on the line; 15-min walk or 5-min bus from the station, bag storage at the station.

b: A palace faced with 8,500 pyramid-cut marble 'diamonds' laid so the light shifts as you walk past — pure Escher/sacred-geometry; the Pinacoteca Nazionale is inside.
g: On the Rome→Venice day — ~10-min walk from Castello Estense, central Ferrara.

n: Ferrara — Via delle Volte & the city walls
b: A long, dark medieval covered street of brick archways, plus 9km of intact Renaissance walls you can walk or bike — UNESCO 'ideal city', flat and bike-mad.
g: On the Rome→Venice day — in Ferrara's compact centre, walkable; rent bikes to ride the walls.
